title: Persistent latent state + adaptive recurrent compute vs a parameter-matched Transformer
question: At the same parameter budget, training data, token budget, optimizer and hardware, does a model that keeps a fixed-size persistent latent state and iterates a shared cell a learned number of times before answering reason better than a standard Transformer -- and where does it lose?

setup.data: benchmarks/microbench.py: tasks state, hops, recall; training on the ID ranges only, a fresh random stream per seed
setup.hardware: CPU, 1 thread per run (GitHub Actions runners or any CPU)
setup.baselines_note: Two baselines: 'transformer' matches Rouge's parameters (205,740 vs 211,373); 'transformer-flops' matches Rouge's compute per example (138 vs ~110-124 MFLOP measured on the ID set). A pilot (40 steps, not evidence) showed Rouge costs ~11x the FLOPs of the parameter-matched Transformer, so a win must also hold against the FLOP-matched one.

predictions.P1_state: Multi-step state, OOD (16-32 operations): rouge >= transformer + 0.20 exact match (mean of 3 seeds) and rouge > transformer in every seed.
predictions.P2_hops: Variable depth, OOD (6-8 hops): rouge >= transformer + 0.10 (mean), and rouge's think steps rise with the hop count (Spearman rho >= 0.6 over hop levels 1-8).
predictions.P3_recall: Long dependency / many facts: transformer >= rouge on recall, ID and OOD. A fixed-size state is expected to lose to attention over the whole context here.
predictions.P4_adaptive: Adaptive halting is not worse than fixed 4-step thinking (OOD all >= rouge-fixed - 0.02), and thinking longer at test time (max 16 steps) does not reduce OOD accuracy.
predictions.P5_compute: Against the FLOP-matched Transformer, rouge is still ahead on the task(s) where P1/P2 hold; otherwise the gain is bought with compute, not architecture.

decision.advance: P1 or P2 holds AND P5 holds for that task: continue with R1.02 (learned halting, compute penalty sweep) and R1.03 (state probes) on this prototype.
decision.fail: Otherwise: do not scale. Diagnose (optimisation, state capacity, halting collapse, read cost) and register a changed prototype as R1.01b.
decision.report: Wins and losses per task, every seed, parameters, disk, state memory, FLOPs, latency and wall-clock -- including where Rouge loses.

not_claimed: Persistent state, recurrence and ACT halting are prior art (see docs/rouge/research/rouge-architecture-r1.md). R1.01 tests whether this combination buys capability per parameter on controlled tasks; it is not a claim of novelty or of general intelligence.
